featured_reviews.name: Sneha Arekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
1) A good yoga teacher who teaches every Asana with right technique and nuances. Detail oriented with the form.

However, at the same time I do feel that her routine of asanas in a given session are not very well spread out or properly curated. She focuses on one part or segment of the body in one session and will conduct multiple asanas to target that particular segment only. The worst are Wednesdays, the reverse back bending day. My first Wednesday session with her gave me such a severe lower back pain at night. And I am NOT a beginner level.
This happened because she over back bended the whole session.
Also this way if you miss or skip a session you missed the exercise for that body part. Doesn't make sense.

I do feel her session routine should be more spread out throughout the body where you hustle every part and segment of your body a little bit in every session.
A Little bit of everything is more required than specific.

2) no yoga warm ups like knee rotation or hip rotation, shoulder rotation etc. she leaves the warm up to us.
Doesn't end every session with Shavasan. Only sometimes.

3) I do feel she would be a good tutor for someone looking for advanced level yoga or wanting to attain a yoga teaching course license themselves.

4) Beginners, middle aged and Seniors can have her trial sessions at your own risk.

5) on the day of my trial session she asked if I am ok with the headstand. Shirshasan. I said I can try but I am not very confident. As I have never got it right so far and have a certain personal phobia about it of breaking my neck.
So I told her to stand right next to me and hold my legs just incase I begin to fall absurdly. Because that break or sprain will cost me a lot. She didn't bother to stand next to me. She watched from the front giving instructions how it is to be done. Or may be she didn't get my message I am not sure.
Eventually when I did something wrong and fell sideways bending my neck a full 90 degree. That was very very dangerous for anybody to break their neck or twist leading to paralysis. By the way I am 5'8" and 75kgs. So that's a huge body on that neck.
Even after that I still joined the class and paid fees next week because I didn't want to judge the class by that one event.

6) she is rude and arrogant. Not always but mostly. I am not sure if that comes from her bouts of mood swings.
I found that very strange personally for a yoga teacher to have that kind of a personality. Has a high pitch voice and tends to yell at times as if teaching primary schools kids.
I was bit surprised no one else seemed to mind it. Or may be they do but they have been with her for a very long time so they are used to it and don't care much. Because she also tends to be the only yoga class in the locality so everyone is just tolerating until something else better comes up.

Her persona or aura is nowhere even near to being pleasant or calm or soothing as you would expect a yoga teacher's to be.

7) before reaching out I had checked the reviews and found only one review 1 star else all are 4/5 stars. I found this absurd. But still gave it shot.
Only now to realise that the 1 star review by Shweta Shriyan is only realistic and rest would be just lobbying or goodwill.
I do resonate with every point that Shweta has listed.

8) Everytime after the class I felt miserable and not rejuvenated. I have been through 8-10 different yoga teachers since last 20 yrs and she is the only unpleasant one I have experienced tille date.
I have attended yoga classes that were conducted so beautifully by the tutor that I left everything else in the world to attend it. I looked forward to it.
With this one I was only waiting for the month to get over.

My stint with her was only for a month and I don't even wish to continue anymore despite having my 1k in 'BALANCE' with her.

But all in all I will still say that she is good yoga teacher at the end of the day. Still worth a shot. Only whether she suits your needs and concerns or not might be a hit or a miss.

Best of Luck.

What is even more worrying is that if this can happen to one member today, it can happen to any member tomorrow. Many experienced gym-goers naturally help beginners with form, technique, or motivation without charging money or claiming to be trainers. Treating such interactions as a business threat reflects poorly on the management’s priorities.

Instead of focusing on member satisfaction, retention, and building a strong fitness community, it appears the emphasis is being placed solely on protecting personal training revenue.

A gym membership is a service paid for by members, not a privilege that can be arbitrarily denied. This incident leaves a very negative impression about the management’s attitude toward its own members.
